title: Enterprise capture & weighted-priority flow for hosted chat streaming + toolchains
creator: Priya Patel
description:
Problem: Enterprise customers submitting hosted-API feature requests for multi-action chat sequences (streaming + tool/function calls + structured outputs) receive inconsistent prioritization and long onboarding loops. Requests come from rentention-critical accounts and platform teams; signals are noisy and often conflict (SLA, regulatory need, expected throughput).

Goal: Create a lightweight capture workflow and a weighted-priority classifier that standardizes incoming requests, surfaces critical signal combinations (security/regulatory + latency SLO + data-sensitivity), and outputs a recommended routing bucket (self-serve backlog, solutions-eng queue, enterprise fast-track). Deliver a clear onboarding checklist and minimal triage steps so PM/SEs can make deterministic decisions within 24h for 80% of requests.

Scope: Hosted API feature requests only (chat streaming, function/tool-calling, structured outputs). Excludes Dedicated/Private deployment engineering work beyond handoff and SLA negotiation. Deliverables: 1) capture form template and webhook to triage board, 2) priority weight matrix and scoring rules, 3) operator UI in Console for manual overrides and notes, 4) playbook for SEs for first-contact onboarding, 5) telemetry/dashboard for request throughput and time-to-first-response.
acceptance_criteria:
1) A JSON schema for the intake form plus validation rules, stored in Confluence and used by the intake webhook.
2) Priority classifier that maps incoming requests to one of three buckets with an explainable score and top-3 contributing signals.
3) Console operator view mock + prototype that allows triage and manual reclassify within 15s.
4) Pilot with three enterprise customers (one fintech, one healthcare, one marketplace) with time-to-first-response <= 24h for >= 80% of submitted requests.
5) Dashboard showing distribution of signals (SLA, data-sensitivity, expected throughput, revenue risk) and time-to-resolution metrics for the pilot period.
comments: 2025-01-28 Priya Patel: Created initial PRD and aligned on scope with Solutions Eng. Highlighted need to catch multi-action requests that use both streaming + tool calls — these have higher operational complexity.

2025-02-03 Diego Alvarez: Drafted intake JSON schema and outbound webhook. Shared with ENG for validation (ENG-34820). Noted ambiguous field: 'expected_concurrency' — ENG requested example values and units.
2025-02-07 Maya Chen (Design): Attached low-fi operator UI for the Console triage pane. Emphasized quick notes and one-click escalate. Will iterate after pilot feedback.

2025-02-10 Solutions Eng sync: Agreed pilot customers: Acme Financial (fintech), MediBridge (healthcare), MarketLoop (marketplace). Agreed pilot acceptance criteria and contact leads. Action: SEs to populate onboard checklist for each customer.

2025-02-14 Diego Alvarez: Implemented priority weight prototype in a spreadsheet. Early rule: regulatory-sensitive + high-throughput => escalate. Trade-off: aggressive escalation increases SE load; adding revenue signal reduces false positives. Seeking PM sign-off on weight defaults.

2025-02-18 Priya Patel: Weight defaults reviewed; small change to favor data-sensitivity over revenue for healthcare verticals. Created Confluence doc for intake flow. Next: engineering grooming to create webhook and storage for intake events (ENG-40105).
notes: Operator flow should be lightweight — primary goal is deterministic routing with a short human-in-the-loop for edge cases. Plan to ship weight defaults and a config UI so SEs can tune per-customer during pilot. Consider future extension to Dedicated/Private routing rules if pilot shows >25% of requests require infra changes.
